pages.title: Get started with ClawPod
pages.description: Create role-based AI Agents and collaborate through chats, files, and tasks.
pages.text: Get started with ClawPod ClawPod lets you create AI Agents for different roles and manage conversations, files, and tasks with your team. Your first steps 1. Create an account or accept your organization invitation. 2. For a new workspace, complete onboarding. 3. Set up an AI credential. Ask your administrator if you cannot access this setting. 4. Create your first Agent and review its role and instructions. 5. Try a small task in a Chat Room and verify the result. Find a workflow Goal Guide --- --- Read, summarize, or create files File formats and artifacts Work on the web Browser and CLI tasks Track team tasks Tasks and Milestones Transcribe a meeting Meeting minutes Set an Agent's role and response style Workspace files Deliver external events Webhooks Manage members, permissions, and costs Organizations, billing Available menus depend on your permissions, organization, plan, and Agent environment. See the feature catalog and help. Use Portal menus and guides to find your starting point. It separates Chat and personal settings from tenant administration.

pages.title: Find Portal menus and guides
pages.description: Separate Chat and personal settings from tenant administrator navigation.
pages.text: Find Portal menus and guides The Chat / Admin switch at the top changes the sidebar. Check the role shown in your account menu first. The management list below reflects a tenant administrator's view; ordinary members may see fewer entries according to their permissions and organization settings. Chat and personal settings Location Purpose Guide --- --- --- Chat → New chat / room search Talk to Agents and find Rooms Chat Rooms, Previous conversations Room → Message search Search loaded messages Message search Room → Open workspace Available PC/ClawPod controls, workboard, Artifacts, and meeting notes Desktop, Outputs, Meeting notes Account at bottom left → Settings Profile, password/MFA, appearance, and notifications Account settings, Security Account at bottom left → Language Portal display language Language settings Top notification button → View all notifications Notification history and delivery preferences Notifications The Chat workboard and the organization Tasks screen in Admin mode are different views. Available workspace tools and counts depend on the selected Room and Agent state. Tenant administrator menus Select Admin at the top. These entries are not a promise that ordinary members have the same menu access. Section Entry Guide --- --- --- Start Onboarding Workspace setup Start Dashboard Dashboard, Usage Management Agents Create, Manage Management Organizations Organizations and members Management Tasks Tasks and Milestones Analytics Overview, Costs Analytics and costs Integrations Webhooks Webhooks Integrations AI Key Management AI connections Platform Announcements Tenant announcements Platform Plans Subscriptions and payments Security IAM Users and policies Security Audit Log Audit history For tenant administrators, Plans opens billing management. This differs from the platform super administrator's plan catalog and pricing editor. Missing menus Check your role, current organization, selected mode, and allowed menus. Ask your tenant administrator if a needed entry is missing. Documents, separate AI Chat/Chat Archive, Settings → Workspace/System, and Monitoring are not baseline customer entry points in this guide. Do not guess URLs or broaden permissions just because an entry is absent.

pages.title: Create an account and sign in
pages.description: Sign up, verify your email, sign in, and recover access.
headings: Create an account and sign in
pages.text: Create an account and sign in Self-service registration requires email verification before sign-in. An invitation can activate your account and membership through its own flow; start from the invitation link if you received one. Sign up 1. Select Sign Up and enter your name, email, and password. 2. Enter your intended use and workspace name for self-service registration. Invitations may prefill these details. 3. Review and accept the terms, privacy policy, and B2B terms when shown. 4. Continue and enter the six-digit code sent to your email. You can paste the code. 5. Use Resend verification code if needed; the resend cooldown is 60 seconds. Passwords require at least eight characters, including uppercase and lowercase letters, a number, and a special character. After verification, administrator approval may still be required. Invitation behavior depends on the invitation conditions. Continue with onboarding or accepting an invitation. Sign in Select Sign In. Use Remember me only on your own device. Accounts awaiting email verification return to the verification screen. Repeated failed attempts may temporarily limit sign-in; use password recovery instead of repeatedly guessing. If MFA is enabled in your profile, enter its six-digit code after your password. If necessary, use Use recovery code. See account security. Recovery codes may not be shown again; keep them private and never place them in Chat or documentation. Reset a password 1. Select Forgot Password? and enter your email. 2. Request a code and enter the six-digit code from the email. 3. Enter and confirm the new password, then sign in. The response is the same whether an account exists or not. Check spam filters if the email does not arrive. There is no per-device session list or remote sign-out UI. If you suspect unauthorized access, change your password, review MFA, and ask an administrator to review access revocation and audit records. For support, share your email, the time, and the error message. Never share passwords, MFA codes, recovery codes, or cookies.

pages.title: Accept an organization invitation
pages.description: Join the intended organization with the account named in your invitation.
pages.text: Accept an organization invitation An invitation link is tied to an email address and organization membership. Do not forward it or accept it with a different account. Accept the invitation 1. Open the link in the invitation email. 2. Review the organization, inviter, and role. 3. Sign in with the matching email address. 4. Accept the invitation. 5. Open Chat and confirm the Rooms and Agents you can access. An account with a different email cannot accept the invitation. For an expired or already accepted link, ask an administrator to check its status. If the email or role is wrong, ask for cancellation and a corrected invitation before accepting. Declining only exits the screen; it does not cancel or expire the invitation. If you will not join or the link may have been exposed, ask an administrator to cancel the pending invitation and issue a new one if needed.

pages.title: Complete workspace onboarding
pages.description: Provide company information and prepare the initial Agents for a new workspace.
pages.text: Complete workspace onboarding The /onboarding flow analyzes a company and prepares its initial Agents. It is separate from ordinary Agent creation. Set up a new workspace 1. Select Get Started, enter the company name and business domain, and follow Continue on each screen. 2. Provide homepage, competitor, or agency URLs as requested, plus any additional requirements. A company or competitor URL is required. 3. Select View Results and review the overview and proposed organization. Select roles and choose Confirm Organization. 4. Enter the provider API key and complete validation. 5. Complete phone verification and follow the preparation states: Preparing Soul.md generation..., Organization established, and Deploying agents.... 6. When the AI organization is ready, open Portal Chat and verify the result. Submitted URLs are used for analysis. Do not include secrets, passwords, API keys, or confidential contracts in the analysis request. Use the matching provider for key validation. See credentials and handling secrets. Partial failures When Some agents failed to deploy. appears, use Retry failed agents to retry only the failed Agents, or create them manually. If onboarding does not appear, the workspace may already be onboarded or the account may be awaiting approval. Check account setup and your first Agent.

pages.title: Create your first Agent
pages.description: Create an Agent, review its instructions, and verify a small first task.
pages.text: Create your first Agent You need permission to create Agents. Ask an administrator if creation is unavailable. Depending on organization policy, use a saved credential or provide one during creation. Start with one clear task, such as drafting a customer support response. Create and verify 1. Open Agent and select Add New Member. 2. Enter a name and select a role preset or a custom role. 3. Choose a model and credential from the options available to your organization and permissions. 4. Review the instructions: task, tone, and actions to avoid. 5. Select Hire This Expert, review the details, and choose Confirm & Create. 6. Open the Agent from the list, check its status and settings, and try a small task in Chat. If creation is missing, check permissions. If a model or credential is missing, check availability and access. If Chat does not work, check the Agent status and ask an administrator to review the connection. Never include credentials or access tokens in Chat, documentation, or support messages.

pages.title: What is an Agent?
pages.description: Understand Agent roles, models, credentials, and tools.
pages.text: What is an Agent? An Agent is a configured unit of work: for example, meeting summaries, customer response drafts, or recurring tasks. Setting Purpose --- --- Role and instructions Define the task and response style Model Supplies the AI model used for the task Organization credential Connects the Agent to an authorized provider Skills and tools Add capabilities that may require installation, connections, and permissions An Agent follows its own policies and connections; it does not automatically inherit every personal permission of its creator. Review important outputs and actions. For example: “Summarize customer requests in friendly Korean and draft a response. Do not assert unconfirmed policies; identify anything that needs confirmation from its owner.” Include what the Agent must not do, when a person should review its work, and information it must not use or reveal. See the feature catalog.

pages.title: ClawPod feature catalog
pages.description: Find a public workflow and check its requirements before use.
pages.text: ClawPod feature catalog Use this catalog to choose a workflow. Availability depends on your organization, permissions, plan, and Agent environment. Portal workflows Goal Requirements and guide --- --- Create or manage Agents Creation permissions and quota: create, manage Chat and exchange files Organization and Room access: Chat Rooms, file formats Read past conversations Accessible Rooms: Previous conversations Track team work Organization access: Tasks and Milestones Create meeting minutes Meeting access, participant consent, and organization policy: meetings Configure AI keys and models Credential and Agent management permissions: credentials, models Configure Agent instructions Workspace files Deliver events Webhook permissions, source, and target: webhooks Manage members and access Organization and IAM permissions: organizations, IAM Review analytics and billing Appropriate access: analytics, billing Manage account security and records MFA, notifications, audit log Agent tasks Task Check first --- --- Files and coding Allowed paths and available tools: CLI work Browser work Browser readiness and site access: browser and web Remote desktop A running, supported Agent: Agent Desktop Memory and instructions Retention policy and scope: memory Image generation and audio transcription OpenAI tools, input rights, and budget: media Specify the target, expected result, allowed changes, and external transfers. State what is unknown instead of assuming readiness. See availability checks.

pages.title: Check feature availability
pages.description: Distinguish visible settings, completed setup, and verified capability.
pages.text: Check feature availability A visible menu or an installed Skill does not mean every operation is available. Check a Portal workflow 1. Find the workflow in the catalog. 2. Check your role, organization, plan, and quota. 3. Follow its AI credential, Agent, or webhook setup guide. 4. Confirm the saved status, then run a small test without secrets. Check an Agent task Confirm the actual tools, file access, AI connection, and organization scope for the target Agent. For example: “Check whether you can read the specified document, summarize its key decisions, and flag unresolved questions.” Ordinary users cannot choose every runtime or tool. Use help when setup is unavailable. This guide is not a complete inventory of runtime tools or a grant of permission. A safely observable, authorized capability can be used even when undocumented. Conversely, do not claim a documented capability is available without verifying it for the current Agent. Do not invent settings, discover secrets or internal paths, or bypass permissions to enable a capability. See how Agents should read this guide. Verify and clean up Check the result, actual changes, failures, and steps that were not executed. Revoke unused connections and webhooks, and handle files and memory according to the retention policy.

pages.title: Browser and web tasks
pages.description: Check browser readiness, site access, and the scope of a web task.
pages.text: Browser and web tasks An Agent equipped with a browser can read pages, navigate, enter information, and inspect results. A lightweight Agent without a desktop is not ready for GUI browser work; confirm its environment first. You need the appropriate site account and permissions, a ready browser, and access to the target URL. Treat login sessions, cookies, and downloads as sensitive data. Ordinary users cannot select every runtime; explain the required task to an administrator when adjustments are needed. Request a task 1. Give the target URL and expected result. 2. Specify whether reading, input, submission, downloads, and external transfers are allowed. 3. Start with a small read-only check. 4. Ask for source URLs, actual changes, and failed or unexecuted steps. Follow the browser and CLI guide. Stop and ask the user when login or human verification is needed. Verify the target Agent's tools and access before requesting browser work. A separate Portal AI Chat menu is not a prerequisite. Instructions are not technical access controls. Follow organization access and external-transfer policies.

pages.title: Image generation and audio transcription
pages.description: Understand Agent media tools and their setup requirements.
pages.text: Image generation and audio transcription Agent image generation and audio transcription use AI tools. They are separate from Portal voice input and meeting features. Before a media task 1. Connect the required OpenAI credential. 2. Verify that the corresponding tool is ready. A saved credential alone is insufficient. 3. Specify the input, output, budget, and retention requirements. 4. Run a small test and check the actual output format. Never put secrets in Chat. Confirm rights to other people's voices and materials. Do not assume results automatically become Tasks; see files and artifacts. For Portal voice input, follow Chat Rooms. For recording and meeting summaries, follow meeting minutes. If processing fails, check the connection, tool readiness, format, and budget. Check whether processing already occurred before retrying. Disconnect unused credentials and remove retained inputs and outputs according to policy.

pages.title: Chat and collaboration
pages.description: Understand Room access, shared files, activity, and Agent delegation.
pages.text: Chat and collaboration Rooms bring users and Agents together within organization and tenant access boundaries. The Room list and available Agents are filtered by your permissions. Authorized users can use direct or group Rooms, messages, attachments, mentions, and read status within the permitted organization scope. Shared files and activity Files in Tasks and documents follow their own format, size, and organization rules. Before sharing, check the audience, workspace or Task association, retention, deletion and download needs, and whether the file contains secrets or customer data. Meeting and activity views show high-level information, not every runtime event. Missing activity does not prove an Agent is idle; check its status and messages. Agent-to-Agent collaboration Finding Agents, creating Rooms, and sending messages require the relevant participant and organization access, Agent authentication, and runtime support. When delegating, specify the receiving Agent, data to share, expected result, and whether external transfer is allowed.

pages.title: Connections and integrations
pages.description: Set up AI credentials and webhooks, then verify each connection.
pages.text: Connections and integrations ClawPod connections include AI credentials and webhooks. Connection Setup and verification --- --- AI provider Credentials and models; test a small Agent response Webhook Webhooks; verify the event and target Image or audio tool Media tools; verify readiness and the actual result Before connecting, check the organization, target Agent, permissions, and data-transfer scope. Enter keys in the designated settings, not Chat, documentation, or Skill packages. Saving a setting or accepting a request does not prove readiness. Test with non-sensitive data and inspect status and errors on failure. Follow the relevant guide to disconnect or remove a connection. Removing it from ClawPod does not necessarily revoke its provider-side key.

pages.title: Skills and tools
pages.description: Check the availability and requirements of tools already provided to an Agent.
pages.text: Skills and tools Bundled tools vary by runtime. Lightweight Agents may lack GUI and some office or media tools. Verify availability before assigning work, including browser tasks. Specify allowed files, commands, browser activity, and external transfers. For example: “Read only this week's CSV files in /workspace/reports , write weekly-summary.md , and do not send data externally.” Connect credentials through settings, not packages or Chat. Available tools do not override policy restrictions.

pages.title: Collaborate in a Chat Room
pages.description: Create Rooms, send clear requests, and use files and meeting features.
pages.text: Collaborate in a Chat Room A Chat Room gives users and Agents a shared conversation context. Access and participants are limited by organization permissions. Prepare a Room 1. Open Chat in the Portal. 2. Create a Room from the left sidebar or select an existing one. 3. For a new Room, choose 1:1 or Group , review participants and the name as described below, then create the Room. Available participants depend on your access. 4. Confirm the new Room is selected and the intended users and Agents are present. 5. Write your message. To clarify the intended Agent, select it from mention suggestions, then choose Send. Room type Participants Room name --- --- --- 1:1 Select the Agent to talk to. Generated automatically. Group Select multiple Agents and optionally add teammates. Optional; leaving it blank generates a name from participants. All participating Agents can receive and process a Room message. A mention clarifies intent; it does not route exclusively to one Agent. If exactly one Agent must work, use a dedicated Room containing only that Agent. Webhook events also arrive as Room messages, so a separate automation Room can simplify operations. Confirm that the message appears and the intended Agent responds or shows a processing state. Sending does not mean completion. If Stop appears during generation, it stops that response. Write a clear request Include the expected output and completion criteria, allowed material or attachments, constraints and prohibited actions, and whether the Agent should ask questions or may make assumptions. Example: “@DeploymentHelper summarize today's deployment failure events. Separate confirmed facts from items needing verification, and never output secret values.” When chat modes are available If the composer shows a chat-mode menu, it offers the modes below. If the menu is absent, follow the normal message-writing steps above. Mode Purpose shown in the UI --- --- Default Follow the instructions provided. Discuss Explore together and refine a plan. Execute Carry out work more systematically. The menu also indicates Shift+Tab for switching in the composer. If mode customization shows additional instructions, it accepts up to 240 characters and states that they accompany every message. Check that the instructions should apply repeatedly and keep sensitive values out. Selecting a mode does not grant tool permissions or authorize external actions. Files and outputs Attach files only within the allowed formats and size limits. Check for personal information, secrets, and customer data before uploading. Uploading does not authorize automatic external transfer or permanent retention. Review generated outputs separately from the conversation and keep important files in an approved organization repository. Voice input 1. Select the microphone on the left of the composer to Start voice input. 2. Allow browser microphone access after confirming it is for dictation, separately from meeting recording. 3. When speech appears in the composer, select the microphone again to Stop voice input. 4. Review the transcribed text and Agent mention, then choose Send. The composer is locked while dictating. Speaking @Agent does not automatically open mention suggestions; check the selected mention after stopping. For microphone, network, or voice-session errors, fix permissions or connectivity before restarting instead of repeatedly sending. Meetings Meeting features include recording consent, transcription, summaries, and discarding minutes. Follow meeting minutes for the procedure and privacy boundaries. Clean up a Room Open the Room's more menu in the sidebar to see available actions such as rename, pin, mute notifications, hide, and delete. Use an action only when it is shown. Before hiding an important Room, confirm how you can find it again. Deleting a Room can affect access to its history. Preserve required outputs and decisions and check whether automation targets the Room before deleting. Adjust Room notification settings when alerts are no longer needed. Find messages Open Search messages or press Cmd+F / Ctrl+F in a Room, then enter a query. Search covers only loaded messages; scroll up to load older history first. Opening search may close the Artifact panel. Chat workspace Use Open workspace at the top of a Room to view its PC control, ClawPod control, workboard, Artifacts, and meeting-note tools. Available tools and Agent counts vary by Room. The workboard is separate from organization Tasks in Admin mode; the panel is not a browser for all Agent files.

pages.title: Find previous conversations
pages.description: Use room search and message search to find accessible history.
pages.text: Find previous conversations Find a Room 1. Select Chat at the top. 2. Enter the Room name in the sidebar's room search. 3. If the recent list does not include it and View all is shown, expand the list. 4. Select an accessible Room to read its history. This workflow does not require a separate Chat Archive menu. Do not guess addresses or IDs for Rooms you cannot see. Find a message Open Message search and enter a term. Search applies to loaded messages, so scroll up to load older history first. See the Chat Room guide. Opening a Room may update its read status. You do not need to delete a Room or change its participants to read history.

pages.title: File formats and Agent artifacts
pages.description: Understand upload formats, preview limits, and generated outputs.
pages.text: File formats and Agent artifacts Uploading a file, previewing it in the Portal, and generating it with an Agent are separate capabilities. Chat attachment formats Chat Room attachments allow up to 50 MiB per file (shown as 50 MB in the UI). Category Supported extensions Portal preview --- --- --- Images .jpg , .jpeg , .png , .gif , .webp , .bmp Image preview; download if the browser cannot display it Documents .pdf , .docx , .xlsx , .pptx , .hwp , .hwpx PDF preview up to 10 MiB ; download the others Text .txt , .text , .csv , .md , .markdown , .env , .log , .ini , .conf , .cfg , .properties Text preview; files over 1 MiB show only the first 256 KiB Data and configuration .json , .jsonl , .yaml , .yml , .toml Download HTML .html , .htm Download; no execution or HTML attachment preview Video .mp4 Download; no in-Portal playback Archives .zip Download Names such as .env and .env.production are recognized. Format support does not authorize sharing secrets: remove API keys and passwords from configuration files before attaching a copy, and follow the secret guide for actual credentials. Supported extensions are case-insensitive and normalize the MIME type even when the browser supplies an empty or different type. Other filenames may be accepted through the legacy MIME allowlist. .svg , .svgz , .js , .mjs , .cjs , .exe , .msi , .com , .bat , .cmd , .ps1 , and .sh are blocked regardless of their MIME type. Renaming an extension neither converts nor validates a file. Task and Milestone attachments Task and Milestone attachments retain their separate legacy MIME allowlist and 50 MiB limit: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, TXT, CSV, Markdown, HWP, HWPX, and ZIP. Chat's additional HTML, MP4, JSON, YAML, and other formats do not imply the same expansion for Tasks or Milestones. Preview boundaries - Text previews support stored MIME types text/plain , text/csv , and text/markdown . Files over 1 MiB show only their first 256 KiB. - PDF previews support files up to 10 MiB. - Image previews support allowed image formats. - Download other accepted formats. HTML attachments are separate from HTML artifact previews described below. A preview is not a security scan or complete file validation. Follow organization security procedures before executing or externally sharing received ZIP files, Office documents, or images. Generated outputs Output Verified path Limits --- --- --- Chat artifact Markdown or HTML download UI Only when the Agent responds with an artifact Meeting result Text or Markdown download UI Requires the meeting and artifact generation conditions Workspace file Ready Agent file/CLI tools Formats depend on tools, image, and policy; not every extension is guaranteed Generated image OpenAI key and ready image-generation runtime Check actual MIME type, storage location, and cost in the result You may request PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or ZIP, but first verify that the selected image, Skill, or runtime has the necessary generator. Accepting a Chat attachment does not prove the Agent can create that format. Open and download Chat artifacts Select an artifact card in a Chat message to open its exact version in the Artifact panel. Choose another version if available. Preview Markdown or HTML, copy Markdown or plain text, or download an HTML artifact as .html and other artifacts as .md . Unauthorized access shows forbidden; a missing version shows not found. Versioned Chat artifacts do not automatically synchronize with Agent workspace files. Example request Create this week's summary as weekly-summary.md and weekly-summary.csv in /workspace/reports . First check the tools and path permissions. Do not overwrite existing files or transfer data externally. Report the paths and validation results when finished. Specify filenames, formats, paths, overwrite rules, and external transfers. See the catalog and browser and CLI guide.

pages.title: Request browser and CLI tasks
pages.description: Scope and verify web navigation, downloads, commands, and file changes.
pages.text: Request browser and CLI tasks Browser control uses the full Agent image; CLI work uses full or lite images. Platform super administrators control image selection. Ordinary users receive an available full image by default; request an adjustment only if the created Agent uses lite or fails browser-readiness checks. clawpod/agent-lite has no Chromium, X11 Desktop, or VNC/noVNC and is unsuitable for GUI browser work. The cli-anything Skill is bundled in full and lite images and prepared at /workspace/skills/cli-anything during boot. For Skills needing a specific CLI package or external service, first configure the dependencies and credentials listed in SKILL.md . Browser requests Browser tasks include opening pages, navigating, typing, clicking, snapshots, screenshots, uploads, and downloads. Full-image Agents use Playwright MCP for browser control and a desktop Skill for GUI desktop control. Include: 1. Target URL and business purpose. 2. Whether the Agent may only read or also enter information and click. 3. The allowed account or browser-profile scope. 4. Whether confirmation is required before submission, purchases, sending, or downloads. 5. Expected output: URLs, summary, screenshots, or downloaded files. Read only this week's report list at https://example.com/reports . Do not log in, enter information, download, or transfer data externally. Return a table of titles and URLs. Cloud does not provide a lifecycle for creating, selecting, and revoking dedicated browser profiles. Treat existing Agent browser state, cookies, and downloads as sensitive. Do not share your everyday browser profile or password manager. Ask for confirmation immediately before payments, account changes, messages, uploads, or downloads that may be hard to reverse or transfer data externally. CLI and file requests Specify the target Agent workspace and allowed paths. Check that the required commands or Skills are actually available. Lightweight Agents may lack desktop and some document or media tools. Work only inside /workspace/project . First show the proposed commands and files. Do not access the network, install packages, delete files, or push to Git. Report inspection results only. For changes, use these stages: 1. Inspect: identify commands, files to read, and expected outputs. 2. Review: confirm the files and external effects. 3. Execute: work within authorized paths. 4. Verify: report changed files, checks, failures, and unexecuted steps. Explicitly authorize high-impact commands such as rm , credential changes, package installation, deployment, Git push, and external API calls, and request confirmation before execution. Retrieve and clean up outputs A customer flow for previewing or downloading Agent /workspace files through Portal Documents has not been verified. Ask the Agent to deliver results as Chat artifacts or Chat/Task attachments, and verify filenames and contents before downloading. Clean up sensitive outputs and browser downloads according to retention policy. Send task requests in Chat , in a Room containing the target Agent. The Agent detail Conversations view is read-only. For failures, share the executed step, target URL or workspace path, a non-sensitive error summary, and Agent status. Do not share raw credentials, browser cookies, or full terminal logs.

pages.title: View Agent Desktop and conversations
pages.description: Use the running Agent Dashboard, VNC Desktop, and read-only conversation history.
pages.text: View Agent Desktop and conversations OpenClaw Dashboard requires a running Agent. Desktop requires a full-image Agent. clawpod/agent-lite has no Chromium, GUI desktop, or VNC/noVNC; confirm a Desktop-capable environment with your administrator before creation for GUI tasks. The standard creation form does not provide a full/lite image selection procedure. Agent details may show Desktop, Dashboard, and Conversations. These expose the Agent's environment and conversation data, so access only the Agents needed for your work. OpenClaw Dashboard 1. Open ClawPod Connection in Agent details. 2. View the iframe or select Open in New Tab. 3. Use fullscreen if needed. The Portal proxy supplies the Gateway token server-side; users do not enter it. Complete authentication first if the Agent is awaiting auth . An unavailable message appears when K8s Desktop is not ready. For Gateway connection failures, the Portal retries loading up to twice before showing an error. Desktop 1. In a running full-image Agent, open Remote Agent PC Control. 2. Open the password-status icon in the PC view. If the state is Password: Not set, select Set Password, enter a password, and Save. 3. If it is Password: Set, use Change to replace it. Remove has not been verified to remove an existing password; do not use it as a way to return to passwordless VNC. 4. Changing the password starts an Agent restart. The viewer loads a new connection after about eight seconds. VNC passwords are managed per Agent; the view shows whether one is set, not its value. Never place the password in Chat, SOUL.md , or AGENTS.md . The viewer shows a connection error if noVNC/websockify is stopped or the Pod is unreachable. Desktop views may expose files, browsers, and sign-ins; exclude sensitive information from screen sharing and recording. Conversations Chat Monitoring separates Rooms with user participants from Agent-only Rooms. Selecting a Room shows its latest 100 messages read-only, refreshed every ten seconds. You cannot send messages or edit Rooms here.

pages.title: Track Tasks and Milestones
pages.description: Use organization boards, comments, attachments, GitHub references, and CSV exports.
headings: Link GitHub issues and pull requests
pages.text: Track Tasks and Milestones Tasks tracks work by organization with grid and table views, Task details, organization statistics, Milestones, and CSV export. Open a board 1. Open Tasks and choose an organization. 2. Select grid or table view. Find Tasks using search and status, priority, and Milestone filters. 3. Open a Task to inspect status, assignee, reporter, due date, activity, comments, attachments, and linked material. Use activity and linked Rooms or events to identify the creating Agent or automation. Do not infer ownership or cause from the title alone. Update status Move a Task on the board or change its status in details. Before marking it Done, check completion criteria, outputs, and the Agent's final result. Multiple users may update a Task concurrently; record the reason for important transitions in comments or activity. Comments and attachments Use comments for decisions, instructions to the owner, and blockers. Authors can edit or delete their own comments. Comments render Markdown and may create notifications. Drag files into attachments or select files to upload. Task and Milestone attachments allow 50 MB per file ; see formats. Download or delete files from the list. Before deletion, check references in comments and external work. Link GitHub issues and pull requests In Task details, select the link action in the GitHub area and enter: 1. Repository owner. 2. Repository name. 3. Issue or pull request number. 4. Reference type: Issue or Pull Request. The Task shows the repository, number, type, and status saved at linking time. You can open or unlink the reference. This does not create, edit, merge, or synchronize the live state of GitHub issues or pull requests. Create a Milestone 1. Select Create Milestone on the organization board. 2. Enter name, description, start and due dates, assignee, reporter, and any attachments. 3. After creation, select the Milestone in each Task's details to associate it. 4. Check progress and the Done count. Removing a Task from a Milestone does not delete the Task. Check ownership and impact before changing or deleting a Milestone tied to a release or customer commitment. Export CSV 1. Apply search, status, priority, and Milestone filters. 2. Confirm there are results; the export button is disabled when there are none. Choose Export CSV in the toolbar. 3. Check the downloaded organization, period, and row count. Exports contain organization operational data. Store them in approved locations and limit sharing. Scope Internal relay of instructions to Agents and automatic escalation are not ordinary board controls. Do not assume Task, Milestone, comment, attachment, or GitHub-reference actions guarantee automatic execution.

pages.title: Create and manage meeting minutes
pages.description: Obtain recording consent, review transcripts and summaries, and deliver or discard minutes.
pages.text: Create and manage meeting minutes Create minutes through a Chat Room's meeting feature. Recording and transcription process personal information; confirm organization retention policy and obtain every participant's consent before starting. Start a meeting 1. Open the Room, open its workspace, and select Meeting. Starting may be restricted in Agent-only Rooms. 2. In the consent dialog, select 15, 30, or 60 minutes . 3. Accept both recording and participant-notification consent items. New meetings use the Portal's default title. 4. Choose Agree and Start. Both consent items are required. Do not use transcription without consent or where recording is prohibited. Review transcription and delivery Read the transcript and organize paragraphs in the Meeting panel while the meeting runs. At the end, choose: - Deliver to Agent: save the transcript, generate a summary, and send transcript and summary artifacts to the Room. - Discard: soft-delete the minutes to exclude them from the archive. The same choice appears when the time limit ends. An empty or unsaved transcript cannot produce a summary. Inspect the content before delivery and confirm the delivery or discard result afterward. Past minutes and summary versions Open past minutes from the Room's meeting history. Finalized minutes show transcript and summary and support summary regeneration. Regeneration saves a new version; check the current version before sharing important decisions. Download transcripts as .txt or .md from the history panel. Preserve required originals and summaries in approved storage before deletion. Deleting minutes records a reason and may make referenced results inaccessible from Chat. Manual review after validation failure If distortion or factual errors are detected, Manual review is required. and Start Manual Review appear. Users who can see the action should: 1. Compare decisions, numbers, owners, and deadlines with the original transcript. 2. Select Start Manual Review. 3. Score M8, M10, M11, and M13 from 0–5, and S3 and S4 from 0–3. 4. Select Submit Review to rerun validation. Scores do not edit the summary. If it is wrong, regenerate from the transcript or follow the correction procedure. Do not raise scores just to pass validation. Errors and privacy For processing errors, inspect the message and meeting status instead of creating duplicate meetings. Recordings, transcripts, translations, and summaries may contain personal or customer data; limit recipients and retention when moving them through Chat, webhooks, or external tools. Meeting-domain validation and summary-quota dashboards are separate operational concerns. Use manual review only when its action is actually shown.

pages.title: Create an Agent and review its configuration
pages.description: Review persona, instructions, resources, and connections before creation.
headings: Create an Agent and review its configuration
pages.text: Create an Agent and review its configuration Creating an Agent requires core:agent:Create and available Agent quota. An Agent is an operational resource with a workspace, instructions, model, credentials, and execution environment. Persona and organization 1. Open Agent → Add New Member. 2. Choose an industry and persona preset, or a blank Agent. 3. Check the name, role, description, and target organization. 4. Check whether an Agent already has the same role. If a duplicate-role warning appears, decide whether to create another Agent or improve the existing one. Duplicates can spread webhook targets, costs, and operational ownership across several Agents. SOUL and instructions Specify goals, permitted information, prohibited behavior, uncertainty handling, and output format. Do not put secrets, API keys, sensitive customer originals, or another user's account information in SOUL. For shell, file, or browser work, distinguish authorized automatic actions from those requiring confirmation. Resources and secrets Before creation, check with an administrator if the work needs browser, desktop, or document tools. Lightweight Agents lack GUI desktop and some tools. Ordinary users create with the provided defaults rather than directly changing the environment. Explain additional tool needs to the administrator. Resources can affect usage limits and costs. In the creation form, review role-specific models and provider authentication in the AI model settings, then configure required connections in service authentication. Use only the purpose-specific authentication inputs in handling secrets. Do not copy sensitive values into unrelated creation fields, Chat, templates, or documentation. For non-sensitive custom settings, follow environment variables. Review and verify 1. Complete required settings and choose Hire This Expert at the bottom. 2. If validation passes, review the organization, role, model, instructions, resources, and connections in the dialog. 3. Select Confirm & Create. 4. On success, the Portal opens Agent details. This confirms acceptance of creation; next check status, organization, a small request in a test Room, required Skills/credentials/webhooks, and Logs/Metrics for errors. Avatar generation for blank Agents is supplementary. Its failure neither proves nor prevents Agent creation success.

pages.title: Manage Agent status and settings
pages.description: Inspect an Agent, control its execution, and verify configuration changes.
pages.text: Manage Agent status and settings Available controls and detail sections vary by permissions and Agent status. Find and inspect an Agent Select Admin → Management → Agents , find the target card, and open View details . Check whether it is running, stopped, or in error before acting. Depending on the Agent, details may show Remote Agent PC Control, ClawPod Connection, AI Resource Settings, Chat Monitoring, Metrics, Config, and Logs. Check AI Resource Settings, Config, and Logs before restarting. Confirm the intended organization, model, credential, and workspace and distinguish recent errors from configuration issues. Start, stop, and restart Use the controls at the bottom of Agent details: - Start runs a stopped Agent. - Stop stops a running Agent. - Restart restarts the environment. These require Agent update permission and can affect running work or conversations. Notify the Room and confirm current work has ended before stopping or restarting an operational Agent. After configuration or credential changes Saving SOUL.md may require a restart. Saving alone does not confirm runtime application; inspect restart warnings or failures and verify status and a fresh conversation. Follow the relevant screen for restart requirements after connection or environment changes. 1. Identify the setting and affected Agents. 2. Save at a safe time. 3. Apply required restarts only as indicated by the screen. 4. Verify status and a small Room request. 5. Check Logs and Metrics for errors. Before deletion Fire or deletion may be irreversible. Check whether the Agent is targeted by Rooms, webhook rules, scheduled tasks, or installed Skills; preserve required workspace documents and outputs; and prepare a replacement Agent and owner. Deletion is also controlled by Agent update permissions. Ask an organization administrator if you lack access or cannot establish the impact.

pages.title: Manage AI keys and credentials
pages.description: Register, connect, rotate, and revoke provider credentials.
headings: Connect OpenAI Codex with ChatGPT sign-in
pages.text: Manage AI keys and credentials A Credential profile in AI Key Management holds sensitive connection data for a model provider or local LLM. It is not a personal password vault or general-purpose secret store. Never copy its values into Chat, playbooks, documents, or logs. See secret boundaries. Permissions and identity Listing, creating, rotating, applying, and deleting can require different permissions. Tenant and platform super administrators may have role-based bypasses; other users need all relevant Credential and Agent actions. Seeing the screen does not grant access to every button. Platform super administrators can filter profiles by tenant. When switching tenants, check the tenant, provider, fingerprint, and number of connected Agents , not just the key name. Register a credential 1. Open Admin → Integrations → AI Key Management → Add Key . 2. Select provider and credential type. 3. Enter a name, then supply the credential or complete ChatGPT sign-in below before saving. 4. Check provider, type, fingerprint, version, and connected Agent count. Options include Claude API key or setup token, OpenAI API key, OpenAI Codex ChatGPT sign-in or auth.json , Google Gemini API key, OpenRouter API key, Ollama server, and OpenAI-compatible local LLM server. Actual options depend on release and permissions. Ollama takes a server address and model, not an API key. OpenAI-compatible local servers can accept an API key if needed. A successful connection test does not prove Agent runtime access; verify a non-sensitive prompt on the Agent too. Obtain provider API keys ClawPod does not issue provider keys. Create one in your provider account or project, store it according to organization secret-handling procedures, and enter it only in the Credential input. Provider Issuing console Value for ClawPod --- --- --- Anthropic Claude Anthropic Console API key; setup tokens can be stored but not bound to Agents OpenAI OpenAI API keys Project API key Google Gemini Google AI Studio Gemini API key OpenRouter OpenRouter API keys OpenRouter API key Choose the intended organization/project and set minimum permissions, budgets, and billing with the provider. The Official console link opens the corresponding issuing page. Provider menus and billing terms can change, so fixed button sequences are not reproduced here. The full value may not be shown again. Never paste it into Chat, Tasks, workspace files, screenshots, or support requests. If exposure is suspected, revoke the old key at the provider as well as replacing it in ClawPod. Connect OpenAI Codex with ChatGPT sign-in OpenAI Codex offers Sign in with ChatGPT (Recommended) and Register auth.json . For an ordinary OpenAI API key, choose OpenAI as the AI service. Signing in to ClawPod is separate from connecting the ChatGPT account an Agent will use. Sign in with ChatGPT — recommended 1. Open Admin → Integrations → AI Key Management → Add Key . 2. Choose OpenAI Codex as the AI service and enter a Key name . 3. Keep Sign in with ChatGPT selected and choose Continue with ChatGPT . 4. Note the Device code and choose Open ChatGPT sign-in page . Sign in to the intended ChatGPT account on the official page and enter the code. 5. Keep the ClawPod connection dialog open. Closing it while waiting cancels the connection. 6. When ChatGPT account connected. Save to finish. appears, select Add Key to save. Completing sign-in alone does not finish registration. 7. Check the saved name, OpenAI Codex provider, Codex Login type, and status in the list. 8. Select the saved Credential in the target Agent's AI Resource Settings , check application results, and verify a small request actually reaches the model. This method does not require finding or copying a local auth.json . Use your own or an organization-authorized account. Keep passwords, device codes, and credentials out of guides and Chat. Sign-in problems - Expired device code: retry to obtain a new code. - Device-code login not allowed: check ChatGPT security settings or ask the workspace administrator about permission. Follow organization policy. See the official OpenAI authentication guide. - Waiting or checking: wait for completion; a failed login is not a saved connection. - Expired connection or sign-in required: open Update for the saved key, complete ChatGPT sign-in again, and save. Check application results for connected Agents too. Alternative: register auth.json If you already signed in with Codex CLI on a trusted device, you can choose Register auth.json . 1. Run codex login on that device and sign in with your account. 2. If using file-based credential storage, paste the entire JSON from ~/.codex/auth.json into the manual input. If you changed CODEX HOME , use that location. 3. Complete the form's format check and save steps, then connect the target Agent. Codex may use the operating-system credential store instead of a file. Do not assume the file always exists; use Portal sign-in above or consult the official credential storage guide. The manual input requires valid JSON with a top-level tokens object, not an ordinary API key. Manual auth.json registration does not automatically verify the ChatGPT connection. Distinguish successful storage from a successful Agent request. Update expired credentials after signing in again. Keep authentication files out of repositories, shared documents, issues, and Chat. Connect an Agent 1. Select the Credential in the target Agent's settings. 2. Confirm the Agent and Credential belong to the same tenant. 3. Check for another credential conflicting in the same runtime slot. 4. Inspect whether application is updated, pending, or failed. 5. For pending or runtime warnings, check status and restart requirements, then verify a small request. Claude setup tokens can be stored, but Agent binding accepts API keys only. To change provider or type, create a new profile and review the binding instead of assuming the old profile can be overwritten. Rotate safely 1. Issue a new secret at the provider. 2. Check the profile fingerprint and Used by Agent list. 3. Open the profile and enter the new value. Provider, type, and profile name cannot be changed in the rotation screen. 4. Verify application results and Agent count, then test affected Agents. 5. Revoke the old provider secret after the new connection works. The Portal does not reveal stored raw secrets. It shows identifying fingerprints and current versions. If a value is lost, issue and replace it rather than trying to retrieve it. Disconnect and delete A profile must have no connected Agents before deletion. Check Used by , replace or remove every binding, then delete. If deletion is rejected, check remaining bindings instead of repeatedly submitting. Deleting a profile does not revoke the provider's API key. For exposure, departure, or contract termination, revoke it in the provider console too. Troubleshooting Check the binding, Agent settings, restart state, then provider account, quota, and connectivity. If problems remain, inspect a safe test Room and Agent logs. For suspected exposure, rotate immediately and restart affected Agents. Creation and rotation rights follow organization policy. Never request or share another member's secret. Encryption-key creation, rotation, and recovery are not verified customer Portal self-service features and are not documented here as operational procedures.

pages.title: Handle secrets and sensitive values
pages.description: Use the dedicated paths for provider credentials and webhook signing secrets.
headings: Register a secret through Chat after creation
Do not store secrets in ordinary content
Agent secret store and internal paths
pages.text: Handle secrets and sensitive values Use Portal Credentials for AI model connections. After Agent creation, you can ask the Agent to register work-related secrets in its secret store when the required tools are available and authorized for the task. Value Input Boundary --- --- --- Anthropic, OpenAI, Codex sign-in or auth.json , Gemini, OpenRouter, local LLM credentials Admin → Integrations → AI Key Management → Add Key Tenant-scoped profiles bound to Agents in the same tenant; see credentials Provider credential entered directly for a new Agent Creation AI model settings / service authentication Direct input for that Agent during creation; use a profile for shared rotation and revocation Signing secret for incoming ClawPod webhooks Webhooks → Sources Plaintext may appear only during creation, regeneration, or rotation; see webhooks Service passwords, API keys, or access tokens needed for Agent work Ask the created Agent to register them in its secret store Register only authorized values; use reference IDs rather than storing values in ordinary memory ClawPod account passwords, MFA codes, recovery codes Dedicated account security or authentication screens Use codes for their intended authentication and follow organization recovery-code storage procedures URLs, project IDs, non-sensitive feature flags Creation environment variables Not a secret storage path; see environment variables Register a secret through Chat after creation 1. Open a dedicated 1:1 Room with the intended Agent. 2. Ask it to register an authorized value, for example: Register this service credential in your secret store with the label report-service for report retrieval. Do not copy it into ordinary memory or documents. Reply only with registration status and the reference ID, never the value. 3. The Agent uses memory secret when available. Confirm ok: true and pointer id in the tool result before treating registration as complete. If the tool is missing or disabled, the Agent should report that instead of claiming success. 4. For later work, refer to the label, purpose, or ID: “Find the report-service secret and use it for the authorized report lookup without displaying its value.” Registration does not automatically configure authentication for every tool. A value sent through Chat may remain in the original message or processing records. Registering it does not automatically delete or redact earlier Chat history. Use an organization-approved way to provide the value and avoid shared Rooms or repeated messages. memory secret search finds reference metadata; memory secret get returns redacted information. Where available, use memory secret update and memory secret delete for update and deletion requests. Deleting a stored secret does not revoke the original token at its external provider. Provider credentials For API keys, issue a credential in the provider's official console; for Codex sign-in, follow the Credential login procedure. Register the provider and type in AI Key Management, bind it only to the intended same-tenant Agents, and test in a small Room. On exposure, departure, or contract termination, issue and apply a replacement and revoke the old value. The Portal does not reveal stored raw credentials. Replace lost values rather than trying to retrieve them. Webhook signing secrets A signing secret verifies incoming requests from a Source; it is separate from provider credentials. 1. Securely store the secret shown when creating the Source. 2. Enter the same value in the external service's webhook settings. 3. If exposure is suspected, rotate or regenerate the Source secret and immediately update the external service. 4. Send a test event to verify the new signature and delivery. Do not store secrets in ordinary content Keep secrets out of SOUL.md , AGENTS.md , TOOLS.md , MEMORY.md , shared Chat, Task comments, meeting transcripts, Skill packages, webhook payloads, and custom environment variables. Do not register another user's auth.json , MFA recovery code, or browser cookie. Do not use internal settings or APIs as a vault. Agent secret store and internal paths The Agent secret store scopes values to the owning Agent. Tool responses return reference metadata and redacted values rather than plaintext. Its implementation stores data at .openclaw/memory-secrets/memory-secrets.json under the Agent workspace. Use the secret tools instead of editing this file directly. The Portal's /agents/:id/secrets is a separate internal API for Agent configuration environment variables. It is not the memory secret store and is not required for Chat-based registration. Do not repeat registered values in ordinary memory, documents, or replies. Verify work results and success or failure status instead.

pages.title: Choose providers and models
pages.description: Configure main, sub, fallback, and heartbeat models with matching credentials.
pages.text: Choose providers and models Agent creation and settings support main , sub , fallback , and heartbeat models. Choices must match actual credentials, the model catalog, and the runtime release. Managed providers Provider Credential Model selection --- --- --- Anthropic API key or setup token Standard selector; Agent binding accepts API keys only OpenAI API key Standard selector OpenAI Codex ChatGPT sign-in or auth.json Standard selector; subscription candidates depend on catalog status Google Gemini API key Standard selector OpenRouter API key Catalog models can appear in the standard selector Local LLM (Ollama) Server URL and model Models can be assigned to roles after a connection test; no API key support OpenAI-compatible Server URL, model, optional API key Models can be assigned to roles after a connection test The Credential dialog has six service choices: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI Codex, Google, OpenRouter, and Local LLM. Local LLM distinguishes Ollama from OpenAI-compatible servers, giving seven runtime provider identifiers. The hosted selector uses the first five hosted providers. See provider API keys or Codex ChatGPT sign-in. Sign in through the Portal or register an existing auth.json . Follow each service's terms. Available models Use the current Portal list rather than a fixed list in documentation. Service and model activation can change. If a model is missing, ask your organization administrator; writing its name in instructions does not enable it. Role Purpose Selection principle --- --- --- main Primary responses and final decisions Balance quality, tool compatibility, and cost sub Research, drafts, and supporting work Can be lighter than main; do not delegate sensitive judgments fallback Alternative when main fails Must have working authentication and access, including another provider's credential if needed heartbeat Periodic check-in turns Choose for short checks; this does not enable a Cloud self-service scheduler Fallback is a usable alternate route, not simply a cheaper model. If it uses another provider, connect both credentials and verify each in a test Room. Configure and verify For a new Agent, select models and credentials during Agent creation. To change an existing Agent: 1. Prepare provider credentials. 2. Open the target Agent's details from the Agent list and edit its AI resource settings. 3. Change providers and models for main, sub, fallback, and heartbeat as needed. 4. Choose a saved key or use the direct key entry field for each provider. Verify the selected credentials are available in the same tenant. 5. Check the impact on ongoing work, then choose the action to save and restart . Choose cancel to leave without changes. 6. Wait until the Agent is available again, then verify model responses and required tools with a small, non-sensitive test request. 7. Track cost, errors, and latency in Analytics. Avoid changing several roles at once when diagnosing problems. Local LLM prerequisites Register an Ollama or OpenAI-compatible server and pass the connection test. If parameter-size information is available, the Portal can assign a larger model to main and a smaller one to heartbeat. Review these assignments for access scope, performance, privacy, and fallback. A successful connection test still requires a real response from the target Agent. Verify server access and model readiness. For other integrations, first confirm a supported Portal setup path; do not guess settings or paste secrets into conversation.

pages.title: Set environment variables during Agent creation
pages.description: Pass non-sensitive runtime settings to a new Agent.
headings: Set environment variables during Agent creation
Add variables to a new Agent
pages.text: Set environment variables during Agent creation Environment variables are name/value configuration for a new Agent. Use them only for non-sensitive service URLs, project identifiers, and feature flags. Enter them in the additional environment variables section of the Agent creation form. Use them for endpoints and settings the environment must read, including a local LLM endpoint verified during creation. Manage provider API keys and shared credentials through Credentials; copying them into several Agents' variables makes rotation and auditing difficult. Add variables to a new Agent 1. Open Agent → Add New Member and configure basic information and models. 2. Expand the additional environment variables section near the bottom of the creation form. 3. Select the add-variable action. 4. Enter the variable name in KEY NAME and its setting in the value field, then complete creation review. Names must start with an uppercase letter or , followed only by uppercase letters, digits, or , such as ACME PROJECT ID or INTERNAL API URL . Values cannot consist only of whitespace. The creation flow passes custom variables to Agent configuration. Users cannot override reserved platform keys such as AGENT ID , organization identifiers, Gateway tokens, and internal API URLs. Selecting a local LLM sets OLLAMA HOST from its connection information. Verify after creation Run a small test and verify the needed setting was read and the external connection works. This guide does not provide a procedure for editing existing Agents' variables. Do not call unexposed management APIs or pass secrets to bypass missing UI. Keep passwords, API keys, access tokens, MFA and recovery codes, customer originals, bulk personal data, and shared provider credentials out of custom variables. Do not copy secrets already written in Chat, Task comments, or workspace instructions. Variables configure behavior; they do not replace instructions. Put role rules in SOUL.md and tool conventions in TOOLS.md. The current Portal exposes these fields for new Agent creation only. For an existing Agent, use the organization's approved creation or operational process to update its configuration.

pages.title: SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, and workspace files
pages.description: Choose the right instruction or memory file and verify changes.
headings: When additional editing tools are available
pages.text: SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, and workspace files Find formats and templates in the workspace file reference. Files have different roles and management paths; saving one does not mean it automatically applies to every conversation. Reading and application - Instruct the Agent to read needed files or explicitly read them with filesystem MCP/CLI. The Portal does not control per-session automatic injection lists. - Instructions supply context; writing a shell command, transfer, or deletion in a file does not automatically execute it or technically enforce approvals and access limits. Follow organization policy. - Long bootstrap files may be truncated by context limits. Put essential rules first and reference separate detailed procedures from AGENTS.md . - Changes do not retroactively alter an in-progress response. Check restart requirements and verify with a new conversation. File roles and management File Purpose Management --- --- --- SOUL.md Role, tone, behavior boundaries Agent → target Agent → Configuration AGENTS.md Repeated workflows and operating rules No direct Portal editor; request a scoped, authorized Agent change TOOLS.md Tool conventions No direct Portal editor; request a scoped, authorized Agent change IDENTITY.md , USER.md Introduction and collaboration preferences Agent file permissions and organization policy MEMORY.md , memory/ .md Long-term decisions and daily/topic records Specify retention and deletion scope BOOTSTRAP.md One-time workspace introduction Follow the bootstrap reference after setup HEARTBEAT.md Short periodic checks First verify heartbeat actually runs on the Agent Edit SOUL.md 1. Open the target in Agent. 2. Expand Configuration and read the SOUL.md preview. 3. Select Edit and update only the needed role, allowed scope, prohibitions, and output format. 4. Select Save and check the success message. 5. Reopen the preview and confirm Security Policy and Sub-Agent Delegation sections remain or have been added. 6. Check Agent status and a small read-only request in a new Room. Inspect warnings and restartFailed ; saving does not prove restart completion. Default security and delegation instructions may be preserved or supplemented on save. When additional editing tools are available The configuration card may also show AI editing and expand controls. If they are absent, use the edit-and-save procedure above. Before applying AI-edited content, review the changes and preservation of existing instructions. After saving, verify Agent status and the result as described above. AGENTS.md and TOOLS.md New Agents may receive default operating instructions. These are workspace documents that authorized file tools can read and update. Review defaults and change only what is necessary. SOUL.md is supplied by runtime configuration for persona and security boundaries. AGENTS.md and TOOLS.md are workspace documents after first boot. Only SOUL.md editing is currently exposed in Portal Config. Do not ask an Agent to overwrite every instruction. Establish purpose, target file, rules to preserve, secret exclusions, and reviewer, then obtain the organization's supported workspace-change procedure. Where content belongs Content File Example --- --- --- Tone, role, uncertainty handling SOUL.md Separate confirmed deployment facts from open questions Repeated work procedure AGENTS.md Check authorization and impact before external changes Tool-specific convention TOOLS.md Confirm the account before opening a customer system Stable team preferences USER.md or MEMORY.md Respond in Korean with a summary followed by open questions Daily investigations and long records memory/ .md Dated deployment-event investigation One-time setup BOOTSTRAP.md Workspace introduction and initial checks Never store secrets, passwords, API keys, OAuth tokens, or unnecessary customer originals in workspace files. Use Credentials and dedicated secret inputs. Scoped requests and verification Propose only the output-format section of SOUL.md . Preserve existing security instructions and show the draft first. Record a lasting team preference as one line in MEMORY.md . Exclude credentials, personal identifiers, and customer originals. Requests still require tool policy and actual file permissions; they do not guarantee a write. The Portal cannot directly verify AGENTS.md , TOOLS.md , or MEMORY.md . Review important changes using the organization's procedure and verification artifacts. Check which file changed, whether its management path is supported, whether security and tenant boundaries are preserved, and whether a new test Room confirms behavior after status stabilizes. Keep detailed manuals separate from short workspace rules.

pages.title: Memory and Agent configuration
pages.description: Understand workspace memory, identity, sessions, and execution policies.
pages.text: Memory and Agent configuration You can ask an Agent to retain work context, subject to its tools and organization policy. The only workspace file currently editable directly in the Portal is SOUL.md . There are no Portal controls to enable, disable, or directly edit memory, AGENTS.md , or TOOLS.md . Follow workspace files. Memory Capability Behavior Conditions --- --- --- Search Find relevant past records by meaning and keywords Runtime memory tools and workspace policy must allow it Read Read needed portions of matching files Search first and minimize the read scope Store Keep long-term preferences, decisions, and context Never store secrets in ordinary memory Session summary May write recent context to daily memory on a new session or reset Not a separately configurable or executable Portal feature Memory is managed workspace information, not hidden model state. Specify both what to retain and what to delete. Use dedicated secret inputs for credentials. Identity and workspace Setting Effect Boundary --- --- --- Identity Name, avatar, introduction Follow organization identity policy Workspace Files and instructions Keep separate from other Agents and tenants Bootstrap documents Initial instructions, persona, and user context Long content can be truncated System prompt Basic behavior and boundaries A complete override can replace safety instructions and requires administrator review Timezone and format Default time presentation Specify the user or organization timezone See the workspace guide for reading and management boundaries. Portal-editable files differ from first-boot files. Sessions and subagents The runtime can create sessions and run subagents. Concurrency, depth, model, timeout, and result notifications follow runtime policy, with no per-user Portal configuration screen. Viewing or messaging other Agents' sessions is also not a separate self-service setting equivalent to ordinary Chat Rooms. High-impact tools Specify targets, changes, allowed paths, and external transfers. Written instructions do not automatically enforce approvals or access limits. Follow organization permissions and data policies and verify actual changes and results.

pages.title: Agent workspace file reference
pages.description: Write instruction and memory files for a clear, limited purpose.
pages.text: Agent workspace file reference File Purpose Reference --- --- --- SOUL.md Role, tone, and judgment SOUL.md AGENTS.md Operating procedures and collaboration AGENTS.md TOOLS.md Tool use and local conventions TOOLS.md MEMORY.md Lasting decisions, preferences, and lessons Memory files BOOTSTRAP.md One-time setup in a new workspace Bootstrap and identity Writing principles 1. Give each file one responsibility: persona in SOUL.md , working rules in AGENTS.md , tool details in TOOLS.md . 2. Write short, verifiable actions, such as checking target, impact, and approval before external changes. 3. Use minimum data and permissions. Never include secrets, passwords, tokens, or customer originals. 4. Instructions do not automatically execute tools. Runtime and organization rules determine actual scope. 5. Verify important changes in a test Room. A file cannot bypass model, tool, or channel permissions. The Portal currently edits SOUL.md . Default AGENTS.md and TOOLS.md are supplied at creation and copied at first boot, but no direct Portal editor has been verified for them.

pages.title: Write SOUL.md
pages.description: Define an Agent role, response style, boundaries, and output criteria.
pages.text: Write SOUL.md SOUL.md describes who the Agent is and how it should judge and respond. Edit it through Agent → target Agent → expand Configuration → preview → Edit. Exact session-context injection timing belongs to the OpenClaw runtime, not a separate Portal setting. Include the role and tasks, language and tone, treatment of uncertainty, consistent output structure, and approval requirements for messages, file changes, and external services. Suggested format Frontmatter can identify the role; the body carries the main behavioral instructions. Save and verify 1. Expand Configuration and read the preview. 2. Use Edit to change only the required sections. The Portal editing limit is 100,000 characters . 3. Select Save and inspect the success message. 4. Reopen the preview and check that Security Policy and Sub-Agent Delegation remain or have been added. 5. Verify Agent status and a small read request in a new Room. Check warnings and restartFailed . Saving may preserve or add security/delegation instructions and require a restart. Saving alone is not proof of runtime application. Removing security sections or permitting secret disclosure is not a supported setup method. Draft with external AI The editor's AI editing action lets you choose Claude or ChatGPT. It sends the entire current SOUL.md and your edit request to that service in a new tab. Results are not saved automatically; review them and manually apply only the needed parts. Do not use this if the document contains secrets, customer originals, personal data, or internal URLs that must not leave the organization. The external account's terms and retention policy apply; ClawPod does not control its processing or responses. Avoid instructions to execute every request regardless of authorization, credentials and customer originals, copied full-length manuals, and cross-organization data access. Put detailed procedures in AGENTS.md or separate documents.

pages.title: Write AGENTS.md operating rules
pages.description: Preserve default safeguards while documenting repeated workflows.
pages.text: Write AGENTS.md operating rules AGENTS.md holds repeated workflows, safety, and collaboration rules. The runtime may copy it into the workspace on first boot; the Portal does not guarantee automatic injection into every session. Describe how to work instead of repeating the persona from SOUL.md . Preserve default rules If empty at creation, ClawPod supplies server defaults and copies them at first boot. Defaults cover tool discipline, avoiding repeated responses, secret protection, confirmation before risky work, and deciding when to speak in group chats. Do not replace them wholesale or weaken rules against credential sharing, unconfirmed destructive/external/financial/legal/out-of-scope actions, invented facts, or repeated messages. There is no verified customer-facing Portal editor. Use an approved workspace procedure, preserve a copy, review the change, and apply the minimum needed. Updated defaults do not automatically update existing Agent workspaces. Suggested structure Use clear headings and instruct the Agent to read the file first when relevant. Before changing it, preserve the old rules, avoid duplicating persona or tool notes, maintain tenant and secret safeguards, and test responses and behavior in a small Room.

pages.title: Write TOOLS.md conventions
pages.description: Document safe tool use without confusing instructions with capabilities.
pages.text: Write TOOLS.md conventions TOOLS.md records local conventions for available tools. It neither installs tools nor grants permissions. When empty, ClawPod supplies mcporter usage and some A2A guidance and copies it at first boot. This is not a complete manual for filesystem, browser, and memory tools. No direct Portal editor has been verified. After first boot, the workspace initialization marker prevents recopying staged files. Change existing workspaces through an approved migration and inspect actual files; do not assume updated defaults overwrite them. Content to include Document approved purposes, targets/accounts/paths to check, where to report results, what to inspect before retrying failures, and data tools must never read or reveal. Writing “use a browser” cannot supply a missing browser runtime, network access, or permission. An available tool also does not authorize every target. Runtime, Skills, credentials, and tenant policy determine actual capability and access. Preserve default discovery and A2A guidance and add only organization-specific procedures.

pages.title: Use MEMORY.md and the memory folder
pages.description: Separate lasting decisions from daily records and exclude sensitive data.
headings: Use MEMORY.md and the memory folder
pages.text: Use MEMORY.md and the memory folder MEMORY.md holds lasting decisions, preferences, and lessons. memory/ .md stores daily or topic-specific details. Content Location Example --- --- --- Stable team preferences MEMORY.md Korean operational reports separating facts, assumptions, and checks Confirmed operating decisions MEMORY.md The organization administrator approves deployments Today's investigation memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md Event investigation and next checks Longer evidence memory/topic.md Links and reasoning for a provider change The Portal does not guarantee that MEMORY.md enters every session's prompt. Instruct the Agent to explicitly read needed memory/ .md files with filesystem MCP or CLI. Suggested format Keep records short and verifiable. When a decision changes, record the new fact and date rather than silently overwriting history. Never record API keys, OAuth tokens, passwords, recovery codes, unnecessary customer originals or personal identifiers, other tenants' access information, or unverified assumptions presented as facts. No independent Portal editor has been verified. Agent memory updates require tool policy and workspace write permission, and the result must be reviewed.

pages.title: BOOTSTRAP.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, and HEARTBEAT.md
pages.description: Understand supporting files for initial setup and ongoing collaboration.
pages.text: BOOTSTRAP.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, and HEARTBEAT.md These supporting files help an Agent understand a workspace and its collaborators. Keep the main role and operating rules in SOUL.md and AGENTS.md . BOOTSTRAP.md A new workspace may receive BOOTSTRAP.md , which guides the Agent to read SOUL.md and AGENTS.md , prepare USER.md and memory, and introduce itself. The Agent is instructed to delete it after setup. Do not treat the deleted file as persistent configuration that returns on every restart. IDENTITY.md This file contains the Agent name, role/theme, and identity expression. The runtime may prepare it at creation. Keep lengthy persona and work rules in SOUL.md . USER.md Store stable context such as preferred forms of address, timezone, and team collaboration preferences. Exclude personal identifiers, contact information, authentication data, and customer data. A lasting preference can also be summarized briefly in MEMORY.md . HEARTBEAT.md This is a short checklist for an Agent with heartbeat enabled. Use short, low-cost checks rather than long-running work or repeated messages. Verify execution permission and schedule availability against runtime and organization policy.

pages.title: HEARTBEAT.md and periodic checks
pages.description: Understand runtime check-ins without assuming a Portal scheduler.
pages.text: HEARTBEAT.md and periodic checks Heartbeat lets an Agent periodically check status. Writing instructions alone does not configure automatic execution or Task creation. No customer Portal controls for heartbeat cadence or delivery policy have been verified. This page describes runtime behavior and HEARTBEAT.md ; it does not promise a default tenant automation feature. Checklist HEARTBEAT.md is a short checklist read when heartbeat runs. It is a new-session bootstrap candidate, but heartbeat-specific instructions may be omitted from normal runs when heartbeat is disabled in runtime configuration. An empty or heading-only file may skip a model call. Keep only necessary checks instead of a long list of situations requiring no work. Execution conditions Whether checks run, their frequency, and alert delivery depend on Agent configuration and readiness. No fixed interval or delivery is guaranteed for every Agent.
