There is no Portal setup procedure for cadence or recipients. Give the responsible operator the Agent and desired check purpose; do not guess configuration files or commands. HEARTBEAT OK and alerts HEARTBEAT OK can acknowledge that no action is needed. It is not intended for ordinary user responses outside heartbeat. For an issue, report confirmed impact, evidence, required approval, and next actions briefly. Avoid repeated alerts and unauthorized external work. Need Approach --- --- Group lightweight checks in one session context Heartbeat Run an independent task at an exact time No current Cloud consumer scheduler setup path; use a separately provided organization scheduler only through its procedure Record completed work and status Task record Task completion may wake a subsequent heartbeat, but heartbeat itself does not guarantee Task creation or exactly-once execution. Use the checklist only where heartbeat actually runs, keep it short, require authorization for external changes, check Room/event history to prevent duplicate alerts, and identify affected Agents and organizations before changing disablement, active hours, or delivery targets.

pages.title: Automation and webhooks
pages.description: Deliver external events to Agents or Rooms and verify processing.
pages.text: Automation and webhooks Use webhooks to send external-service events to an Agent or Chat Room. Configure the source, destination, and processing instructions, then verify a test event. Component Role Check --- --- --- Source Event origin Organization, source type, and signing secret Rule Receiving Agents or Rooms Same-tenant targets, conditions, and delivery limits Playbook Instructions sent to the Agent Expected result and permitted actions/data Event Receipt and delivery record Success/failure and the target's actual response Follow webhook setup. Test with non-sensitive data and confirm the Event record and target Room. Receipt alone does not guarantee completed Agent work or automatic retries. On failure, inspect the Event, destination, and Agent status. Check for already executed work before resending. Disable the Source or Rule to stop new processing. Before deletion, review connected services and required settings. Update the sending service too when rotating secrets. HEARTBEAT.md provides instructions for Agents using periodic checks; Tasks and Milestones track work and deadlines. Writing a file or due date does not schedule execution at a specific time.

pages.title: Send webhook events to an Agent
pages.description: Configure Sources, Rules, and Playbooks and verify delivery.
headings: Send webhook events to an Agent
pages.text: Send webhook events to an Agent This workflow sends external events to a chosen Agent or Chat Room. Sources with a signing secret and verifier validate signatures. Before starting, obtain Source and Rule creation permission, choose the receiving organization and Agent/Room, and confirm the external service supports an HTTPS webhook URL and signing secret. Minimize recipients and Playbook content because payloads may contain customer data. Create a Playbook 1. Open Webhooks → Playbooks → Create Playbook. 2. Enter Name and Content. Use Preview or Split to inspect Markdown if needed. 3. Select Save and confirm the new list entry. Playbooks can be attached to both Sources and Rules and are added to event messages. Example: “On a deployment failure event, summarize the impact. Do not guess unconfirmed causes; list the checks still needed.” Create a Source 1. Open Webhooks → Sources → Create Source, choose a source type, and continue. 2. Enter Name and the target organization. 3. Configure a Source Playbook, rate limit, secret generation, and signature method as needed. 4. Select Create Source. 5. In the final integration guide, separately copy the webhook URL and signing secret if shown into the external service's settings. Plaintext secrets may appear only during creation, regeneration, or rotation. Store them according to organization policy, never in documents or Chat. Choose targets with a Rule 1. Open Webhooks → Rules → Create Rule. 2. Choose Name, Source, and Target Type, and add event conditions. 3. Select one or more Agents or Rooms in Target. 4. For multiple targets of the same type, choose broadcast or round-robin. 5. Configure a Rule Playbook, cooldown, and hourly limit if needed. 6. Select Create Rule at the bottom and confirm the Rule appears. Source and targets must be in the same tenant. The operator manages organization separation by selecting the correct Agents and Rooms. Test and verify Send a test event from the external service and check: 1. Receipt in Webhooks → Events. 2. For an Agent target, delivery to that Agent's webhook Room and an executable Agent state. 3. For a Room target, a system message in the selected Room and the necessary participants. The Agent receives the Source, Rule, event ID, JSON payload, and attached Playbook instructions as a message. Stop, rotate, and recover Set the Source or Rule inactive to stop new events. For exposed secrets, rotate or regenerate the Source secret and immediately update the sender. Preserve Source, Rule, and Playbook configuration before potentially irreversible deletion. No user-operated replay endpoint or automatic delivery retry has been verified for the current ingress. Inspect Event records, the target Room, and Agent status; recovery may require sending a new event from the external service.

pages.title: Manage account and organization settings
pages.description: Understand personal preferences and organization membership changes.
pages.text: Manage account and organization settings Personal settings apply to your account. Organization and membership changes can affect other users and Agents; check the scope first. Personal settings Open your account name at the bottom left → Settings and choose: - Profile for profile, password, and MFA settings. - Appearance for Light, Dark, or System theme. - Notifications for preferences and notification history. Where Save appears, confirm saving succeeds. After password or MFA changes, check your devices and recovery method. Agree with the team which critical alerts, such as webhook failures and Task changes, must remain covered before disabling notifications. Portal language Open your account name → Language and choose an offered language. A mark identifies the selected language. This changes the Portal language separately from the Korean/English selector on this guide website. The available choices can depend on your environment. Organizations and membership Authorized users can create organizations and manage user/Agent membership. 1. Open the target organization. 2. Review members, Agents, roles, and access. 3. Add members or adjust roles with minimum necessary access. 4. Before removal, hand over owned Rooms, Tasks, webhook settings, and Agent operations. Creation depends on tenant quota and plan. Removing membership may remove organization data and feature access. Notification history Use type/severity filters and mark one or all notifications read. Check linked Room, event, and Task originals before marking critical alerts read. For the currently exposed actions and delivery settings, follow notification management. Tenant withdrawal and platform changes Tenant administrators may see a withdrawal flow. It can stop related Agents and sign out members. Verify retention, contracts, and recovery windows before using it. Tenant creation/restoration/deletion, plan catalogs/prices, and platform language administration are platform super administrator features outside ordinary organization management. Follow separate approved administrator procedures.

pages.title: Secure your account and manage MFA
pages.description: Configure MFA, change passwords, and understand administrator resets.
headings: Secure your account and manage MFA
pages.text: Secure your account and manage MFA A ClawPod account can access Agents, credentials, organization data, and automation. Enable MFA and store recovery methods securely. MFA 1. Open Profile in settings. 2. Review MFA status and follow setup or disablement. 3. During setup, verify activation with a six-digit authenticator TOTP code. Store recovery codes securely; do not enter one merely as a test. Never store authentication or recovery codes or passwords in Rooms, webhook payloads, Task comments, or templates. A recovery code is consumed immediately when used to sign in. Verify the authenticator on a new device before replacing the old one. Password and profile 1. Enter Current Password and select Verify. Wait for the verified state. 2. Enter New Password and Confirm Password. Use at least eight characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a special character. 3. Select Save Changes. After completion, sign in with the new password only on approved devices. Keep profile information current. Do not reuse passwords or share team accounts. Administrator resets Authorized administrators may send password-reset emails or reset MFA from IAM user details. Availability depends on the target's system role and the requester's permissions. Verify identity and authorization first, then notify the user through a safe channel. Reset is a support feature, not a way to access another person's account. For suspected compromise, update password/MFA, rotate connected credentials, and review Audit Log changes. Ask the organization administrator to review account access revocation and affected Agent operations if needed.

pages.title: Manage notifications
pages.description: Review notification history, delivery preferences, and panel actions.
pages.text: Manage notifications Open preferences Open your account name at the bottom left → Settings → Notifications , or use the top notification button and View all notifications . Choose the in-app and browser push preferences offered by the screen. Push requires permission in the current browser and site; another device or browser may require its own permission. If push is unavailable, check browser and operating-system notification settings. Types and history Available notification types depend on your role. Enable or disable only those shown to you. Ensure important alerts remain covered before disabling them. Use type and severity filters in the full list, open the linked item when needed, and mark individual or all notifications read. The full list does not offer deletion. The popup opened by the top notification button has a separate Delete notification action for each item. Notification actions do not delete the original Room, Task, Agent, or webhook data. Opening a Room may also update related read status.

pages.title: Account and organization administration
pages.description: Find guides for members, access, notifications, usage, and subscriptions.
pages.text: Account and organization administration Administration features depend on your role, organization access, plan, and limits. If a menu is missing, first verify the account and organization. Area Workflow Guide --- --- --- Organizations and members Create organizations and connect users/Agents Organizations Access Attach Policies and inspect effective permissions IAM Security Passwords and MFA Account security Notifications Types and delivery preferences Notifications Audit Read and export permitted change records Audit Log Activity and cost Accessible Agent activity, conversations, and costs Analytics, Dashboard and Costs Subscriptions and limits Status, changes, cancellation, and usage Billing, Workspace usage Before changing settings, verify the organization and target users/Agents and grant only necessary access. Member removal, disconnection, and subscription changes can affect existing work; follow each guide's conditions and verification. For errors, check the target, limits, and error message before broadening permissions. Platform-wide settings and operational recovery are outside this public organization-user guide.

pages.title: Create organizations and manage members
pages.description: Connect users and Agents with appropriate membership and review deletion impact.
pages.text: Create organizations and manage members An organization groups users, Agents, Rooms, Tasks, costs, and analytics. Creating one or changing membership can change others' access. Create an organization 1. Open Organization. 2. Select Create Organization. 3. Enter Name and optionally Description. Check tenant quota first. 4. Select Create in the dialog. 5. Verify the saved result and the new organization card with its users and AI Crew in the organization list. Creation requires core:org:Create and available quota. Define real ownership, data, and membership boundaries instead of treating a renamed organization as a replacement for an existing one. Add users and Agents 1. Open Admin → Management → Organizations and select the target card's Invite User entry to open Add Member . 2. Choose Add User or Add Agent, search, and select one or more targets. 3. For users, choose admin or member , then add. Add Agents after selection. 4. Verify the success message and the added member in the card's users or AI Crew area. To edit an existing member's role, open the organization card to view its details. In the member and role management table, select the pencil icon in the user's row. Choose admin or member in the role editor and save, or cancel to leave without changes. To remove membership, select Remove Member and confirm removal in the dialog. Although the card entry says Invite User , this dialog adds existing users to an organization. It is separate from new-account invitations, resending, or cancellation. Only platform super administrators can assign or change Inspector roles. Agent membership Connect Agents from organization details. Unassigned Agents may show operational warnings; assign an appropriate organization after creation. Before moving or removing an Agent, verify continued Room and webhook-rule access, Task and workspace-document ownership/access, and credentials, Skills, and owners in the new organization. Delete an organization 1. In Organization, select the target card's delete action. 2. Confirm Delete Organization. 3. Check the success notification and removal from the list. Deletion affects user and Agent data access and has no restore procedure in this screen. Review members, Agents, Rooms, Tasks, webhooks, and workspace documents and preserve required data in approved storage. Ask a tenant administrator if access or impact is unclear.

pages.title: Manage IAM, Policies, and roles
pages.description: Assign direct Policies and inspect effective access within Portal boundaries.
pages.text: Manage IAM, Policies, and roles IAM controls actions on Agents, credentials, Rooms, webhooks, and organization data. Even a small permission addition can affect a tenant or organization; grant minimum necessary access. Portal scope Opening IAM requires Policy read access. User management can show or manage profiles, status, last sign-in, organization memberships, Agent assignments, direct Policies, effective permissions, user creation/invitations/updates/deletion, and password-reset email or MFA reset where authorized. Creation/deletion and Policy attachment/detachment require separate actions. Visibility does not imply write access. Role information Scope Principle --- --- --- Platform role Platform or tenant administration System roles such as super administrator and tenant administrator may not be direct-Policy editing targets Organization membership role One organization Use roles such as admin and member for membership scope Direct Policy Fine-grained user access Include only required actions and resources Policy details currently manage direct user attachments. Group and reusable Role APIs may exist in code, but are not exposed and verified customer Portal workflows. Do not treat them as public procedures or call internal APIs directly. Attach a Policy 1. Open user management under the administrator security menu. In the Users tab, choose the manage action for the target user. 2. In the user details, select the edit action in Direct Policies . The policy editor opens inline. 3. Check required Policies and uncheck unnecessary ones, then save changes. Choose cancel to leave without changes. 4. Review the result and permission sources in Effective Permissions . 5. Test the minimum required task with the target account. Detach unneeded access from the same view. First check whether it would interrupt webhook management, Agent operations, exports, or credential rotation. Custom Policies Creation and deletion are platform super administrator operations. The creation screen accepts name, description, and a Policy document using visual or JSON editing. 1. Open IAM → Policies → Create Policy and enter a name. 2. Choose a Quick Start template or at least one action in Visual editor . 3. Limit resources to the intended tenant and organization. In JSON editor, validate JSON and every statement's actions. 4. Select Create Policy . 5. Attach to one test user and check effective permissions and behavior. 6. Record impact and a rollback owner before expanding to necessary users. System Policies may not be editable or deletable. Deletion can immediately change attached users' access; inspect attachments and effective permissions first. Diagnose access Check organization memberships, platform role, direct Policies, the source of each effective permission, tenant/organization scope, and plan/quota limits. Identify the exact resource and action before increasing access. Avoid temporary super administrator grants; reproduce with a test account and minimal Policy.

pages.title: Manage tenant announcements
pages.description: Create and target announcements when the tenant administrator menu is available.
pages.text: Manage tenant announcements This guide is for tenant administrators who can see Announcements . It is not a task for ordinary members without announcement permissions. Compose an announcement 1. Select Admin → Platform → Announcements . 2. Choose Create Announcement . 3. Enter a title and Markdown content, within the displayed limits of 500 and 10,000 characters respectively. 4. Review start/end dates and whether it is active. 5. Optionally enter a link. The form accepts a link starting with /portal/ or https:// . 6. Review the tenant and organization targets. Choose all or specific organizations within your permitted tenant scope. 7. Review content, recipients, and dates before creating it. Use Cancel to leave without creating an announcement. Check the saved result and the total, active, and scheduled counts in the list. An error is not a successful save. Whether a recipient sees the announcement also depends on the targeting and time conditions. A page description referring to the whole platform does not extend a tenant administrator's reach into other tenants. Keep passwords, credentials, and personal data out of announcements.

pages.title: Read and export Audit Log
pages.description: Investigate changes and export only the necessary records.
pages.text: Read and export Audit Log Audit Log records important permission, Agent, and configuration changes. Read and export permissions may be restricted separately. Find records 1. Open Audit Log . 2. Filter by date, event type, Agent, and severity. 3. Open an entry to inspect before/after differences and related information. Narrow time, organization, and Agent scope first. Broad exports may include other users' operational information. Export When filtered results exist, choose CSV or JSON: 1. Apply necessary filters. 2. Recheck count and scope. 3. Select CSV or JSON . 4. Save to an approved location and record recipients and retention period. Treat exports as access-controlled operational data. Do not upload them to Chat Rooms or public issues. Dispose of them according to retention policy after the investigation. Check who performed which action, affected resources and organizations, sensitive before/after values, and whether follow-up requires access revocation, credential rotation, or Agent restart. Audit Log assists investigation; it does not automatically roll back changes. Verify current settings and affected users/Agents before reversing anything.

pages.title: Review analytics and LLM costs
pages.description: Use the Analytics menus in Admin mode to review activity and model costs.
pages.text: Review analytics and LLM costs Open analytics Select Admin at the top, then open the following entries under Analytics . Visible menus and data depend on your role and permissions. Menu What it shows --- --- Overview Active Agents, processed messages, total cost and tokens, LLM calls, conversations, and organization metrics Costs Total cost, model/organization/Agent costs, and daily spending Choose the period in each view. Compare the same period and organization scope. LLM usage costs are separate from subscription payments; use plan management for the latter. Investigate changes 1. Review activity and error rates in Overview. 2. Compare cost changes with model, Agent, and usage changes in Costs. 3. If the cause remains unclear, review Agent details, logs, and related webhook Events. Metrics alone do not establish a failure's cause or authorize configuration changes. Platform operations menus such as Monitoring and System are outside this customer workflow.

pages.title: Review Dashboard and costs
pages.description: Check activity and resource usage, then review LLM costs.
pages.text: Review Dashboard and costs Dashboard and cost entries depend on role and permissions. Start in Admin mode. Dashboard 1. Open Dashboard in the sidebar. 2. Choose the reporting period at the top. 3. Review quick insights, top Agents, recent activity, and workspace usage. 4. Open an Agent link or Management → Agents for more detail. Workspace usage shows the tenant plan and member, organization, and Agent counts and limits. No separate Settings entry is required. LLM costs Open Analytics → Costs to review total costs and model, organization, and Agent breakdowns for the selected period. See analytics and costs. LLM usage analysis is separate from subscription payment history. Align the period and scope when comparing metrics.

pages.title: Review plans, subscriptions, and payments
pages.description: Use plan management to review tenant billing and resource usage.
pages.text: Review plans, subscriptions, and payments This guide is for tenant administrators with subscription management access. Ordinary members who cannot see the entry should contact their administrator. Open billing 1. Select Admin at the top. 2. Choose Platform → Plans in the sidebar. 3. In the billing screen, review your plan, billing information, and resource usage. 4. Find Payment history on the same screen. Review date, plan, billing cycle, changes, and amount; open an item's details when available. You do not need a separate payment-transactions sidebar entry. Platform-wide transaction administration differs from tenant subscription history. Use Costs for LLM usage analysis. Before changing a subscription Available buttons depend on Free/paid status, payment provider, and subscription state. Use only the upgrade, adjustment, cancellation, or resumption actions offered by your current screen. If an action is absent, contact the billing owner. Before confirming, check: - Target plan, monthly/annual cycle, and displayed amount. - Current users, organizations, and Agents against the new limits. - Effective date, next billing date, or cancellation date. - Effects on working Agents and data you need to retain. Review the payment or change confirmation before submitting, then return to billing to verify the subscription and limits. Scheduled cancellation does not mean data deletion or immediate termination. Errors If an error appears or billing/subscription state is unexpected, contact the billing owner instead of repeating payment. Treat the actual billing screen and payment result as authoritative, not guide examples or an Agent's quoted amount. Do not paste payment or authentication information into Chat.

pages.title: Check usage and Agent status
pages.description: Review usage in Dashboard and plan management, then investigate Agent issues.
headings: When an Agent does not respond
pages.text: Check usage and Agent status Check resource usage 1. Select Admin at the top and open Dashboard . 2. Find Workspace Usage and review the plan, member, organization, and Agent counts and limits. 3. If you manage subscriptions, open Platform → Plans . The billing screen also shows resource usage for organizations, users, and Agents. These counts describe tenant resources, not an Agent's file workspace. You do not need a separate Workspace entry in Settings. If a limit blocks creation, compare the required resources with the current limits and discuss cleanup or a plan change with your tenant administrator. When an Agent does not respond 1. Open Management → Agents and check its status. 2. Open its details and review the available metrics and logs. 3. For webhook requests, check Integrations → Webhooks → Events . 4. If several Agents are affected, report the time and scope to the operations contact. System and Monitoring are not required steps in this customer workflow. Do not guess addresses for menus that are not shown. If a menu is missing Dashboard, Agents, and plan management depend on your role and allowed menus. Use the Portal menu guide and ask your tenant administrator to check usage or status when you cannot access those views.

pages.title: Help
pages.description: Start troubleshooting permissions, Agent creation, and connections.
pages.text: Help If something goes wrong: 1. Verify the current organization and account. 2. Check roles and permissions if a menu or button is missing. 3. Confirm the required model and credential are connected for the organization. 4. If the problem continues, send the time, attempted action, error, and Agent name to your organization administrator or support. Do not include secrets, access tokens, API keys, or full customer conversations. Common questions - Cannot create an Agent: first Agent. - New to Agents: what is an Agent?.

pages.title: How Agents should interpret this guide
pages.description: Resolve differences between documented workflows and verified runtime capability.
headings: How Agents should interpret this guide
pages.text: How Agents should interpret this guide Product documentation describes official consumer workflows; it does not fully replace actual tools, permissions, or connection state. Trust order 1. The current user request, explicit authorization, and organization policy. 2. Permissions, tools, and runtime state verified in the current session. 3. Safely readable resources and connection state. 4. This guide and its capability tables. Prefer safely verified facts in the current environment when documentation differs. A capability's existence does not itself grant execution permission or user approval. Undocumented capabilities “No official consumer lifecycle” means no verified customer Portal creation, configuration, and revocation flow. “Available on the current Agent” means safely verified tools/runtime plus the necessary permissions and approval. In the latter case, explain availability and perform the requested scope after the smallest read-only/no-op check. For example, an existing browser tool can perform an authorized limited URL read even without a Portal setup screen. Boundaries - Do not exceed permissions, organization policy, tenant boundaries, user authorization, or credential scope because a tool exists. - Do not discover secrets, directly call internal APIs, or force-enable hidden features through configuration or shell commands. - Follow explicit user scope for external transfers, file changes, browser input/submission, installation, and deletion. - Do not guess when docs and runtime differ. Separate verified state, the smallest possible action, and why something cannot be checked. Suggested response Report the verified capability, allowed task scope, remaining restrictions or approval needs, and the next safe check or user choice. See availability for the distinction between consumer setup and runtime capability.

pages.title: ClawPod Guide tools for Agents
pages.description: Search and read public product documentation through the read-only MCP server.
pages.text: ClawPod Guide tools for Agents clawpod-guide is a read-only MCP server registered in ClawPod Agent images. It remotely reads main of the public Wondermove-Inc/clawpod-guide repository without cloning it or saving documents in the Agent workspace. It requires a running image containing the server and runtime network policy allowing GitHub. Existing Agents do not gain it until replaced/restarted with a supporting image release. Registration The image's default MCP configuration registers clawpod-guide automatically. No Portal API key or manual MCP server address is needed. First check whether it appears in the current tool list. If it is missing or GitHub is unreachable, do not search for installation files or copy documentation into the workspace. Report the available tools and failure and narrow the task to user-provided documents or other permitted sources. APIs search clawpod guide Find relevant pages. Each call reads the public repository's search index and returns paths, titles, descriptions, and relevant context. Input Required Meaning --- --- --- query Yes Natural-language feature, setting, or task limit No Default 5, maximum 10 results Search results alone do not establish setup, permissions, or support. Read the returned page next. read clawpod guide Read lines from a page returned by search or section listing. Arbitrary URLs and paths outside the repository are not accepted. Input Required Meaning --- --- --- path Yes Exact returned path, such as guides/manage-agent start line No First line to read; default 1 max lines No Default 200, maximum 400 If the response includes next start line , use it with the same path to continue. list clawpod guide sections List sections and pages. Supply group to narrow to one section. Use this when the query or documentation scope is unclear. Agent workflow 1. Search for relevant pages. 2. Read the best match for procedure, prerequisites, and limits. 3. Prioritize current authorization, organization policy, and actual tools/permissions over documentation when assessing execution scope. 4. If a page or runtime tool is missing, do not conclude the capability is impossible; follow safe interpretation. The tools only read documentation. They do not access or modify secrets, tenant data, Agent settings, or external services.
